title: Client-side throttling & prefetch adapter for embeddings + rerank across SDKs
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Goal: deliver a cross-language client-side adapter that provides safe prefetching, adaptive throttling/backpressure and ergonomic streaming iterators for Embeddings + Rerank endpoints in Python, TypeScript, and Go. The adapter should: 1) preserve API parity across SDKs; 2) work with both batch/pagination APIs and streaming token flows; 3) be friendly to memory-limited environments (mobile/edge); 4) integrate with our retry and idempotency policies. This ticket covers design, prototypes in each language, perf comparison, and integration tests.

Why: Customers repeatedly ask for "streaming-friendly" embeddings + rerank helpers that hide batching/ pagination complexity while providing predictable latency and cost. Existing SDK helpers are focused on simple pagination or naive prefetch; they either overload memory or fail gracefully under token-surge workloads. This adapter balances throughput and latency via an adaptive window and backpressure signals from the network and runtime.
acceptance_criteria: Single semantic API documented and implemented in Python/TS/Go: an async iterator (or language equivalent) that yields rerank candidates and embedding pages with metadata (original_index, token_count, model, page_token)
Adaptive prefetch defaults safe for 2GB ephemeral memory (desktop) and a tuned low-memory mode for 256MB environments
Retries adhere to existing SDK retry profiles; idempotent batching guarantees no duplicate re-ranks across retries
Comprehensive unit + integration tests for pagination, partial failures, and streaming cancellation
Benchmarks showing <=15% latency regression versus raw single-call loop at p50 for 100 concurrent clients, and >=2x throughput improvements for batched flows under steady state
Docs + examples for Python, TypeScript, and Go shipped with the SDKs and a short migration guide for users of the older pagination helpers
technical_notes:
Design summary: provide a small adapter object per SDK that composes three concerns: (A) prefetcher that issues N inflight requests but respects an adaptive window based on observed response latency and configured SLO, (B) local in-memory queue with per-item metadata and soft memory accounting, (C) backpressure hooks into the host language's cancellation/abort patterns (asyncio.CancelledError / AbortSignal / context.Context). The adapter must expose: .iterator() (async for/for await/chan), .close()/cancel(), and a tunable policy object for batch_size, max_prefetch_bytes, and max_inflight_requests.

Edge cases: large rerank payloads (per-item embedding >128KB) require streaming deserialization and immediate eviction policies; Python prototype needs a memory pool for embedding buffers to avoid GC spikes; Go implementation must avoid copying slices when pushing through channels; TypeScript should stream-transform fetch responses when using node-fetch/undici to prevent buffering whole pages.

Retries: follow SDK standard exponential backoff with jitter; prefetcher must retry transient failures (5xx, 429) but not re-run requests that already committed IDs unless idempotency key present. For rerank flows where server-side partial success is possible, adapter will surface partial results and an error field on the yielded item.

Telemetry: instrument inflight_count, avg_prefetch_latency_ms, bytes_queued, retry_count and yield_latency_ms. Add tags: sdk_language, endpoint (embeddings|rerank), client_mode (lowmem|default).
implementation_steps: Spike: implement minimal prefetch + iterator prototype in Python (asyncio) and run with internal rerank workload (Mar 2 - Mar 4)
Parallel prototype: TypeScript async iterator using undici stream pipeline (Mar 3 - Mar 6)
Go prototype using buffered channels and context cancellation (Mar 4 - Mar 8)
Perf harness: create load generator that simulates PLG bursty patterns and steady-state batching; collect p50/p95 and memory profiles (Mar 5 - Mar 9)
API review with SDK owners and docs review (Mar 9)
Address GC/memory issues and add memory pooling in Python; reduce copy paths in Go; split Node pipeline into streaming and buffered modes (Mar 10 - Mar 13)
Add unit + integration tests, CI jobs and feature flags for staged rollout (Mar 13 - Mar 16)
Docs, examples, changelog, and publish SDK minor versions (Mar 17 - Mar 20)
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind sdk.featureFlags.client_prefetch_adapter=false by default. Staged rollout: internal teams opt-in -> beta customers -> global enable. Monitor telemetry and set automated rollback threshold: error_rate > 1% or median memory > configured limit for 5m window. Communicate migration path: existing pagination helpers will be deprecated after one minor release and compatibility shims will be provided.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Asha Kapoor: Completed Python spike. Baseline adapter yields items as (index, vector, meta). Observed GC spikes when >10k embeddings buffered. Next: add memory pool and soft cap eviction.

2026-03-04 - Miguel Santos: TS prototype working with undici streaming; discovered edge case where server returns partial page and then 5xx. Decided to surface partials with error metadata rather than swallow them.
2026-03-06 - Jordan Lee: Go proto finalized basics. Channel buffer sizing heuristic set to max(4, cpu_count/2). Need to ensure slice reuse to avoid copies in rerank path.

2026-03-08 - Product (Camila Ortiz): Requested explicit 'low-memory' preset to ship with SDK and a simple migration note. Also asked to include example calling pattern for long-running background workers.

2026-03-09 - QA (Ravi Patel): Added integration test plan for cancellation and retry interleaving. Noted a flaky case where cancel happened during in-flight retry; will require clearer abort semantics in the SDK policy.
2026-03-10 - Miguel Santos: Working on Python memory pool. Started porting adapter to existing iterator helpers so other SDK features (prefetch cache warmers, rerank debug traces) can hook in.
notes_for_reviewers: API ergonomic goal: keep surface minimal. Python: async for item in adapter.iterator(batch_size=32): ... ; TS: for await (const item of adapter.iterator({batchSize:32})){ } ; Go: for item := range adapter.Iterator(ctx, 32) { } . Look for edge-cases in memory-limited CI nodes and ensure telemetry tags are comprehensive.
final_delivery_checklist: All three SDKs ship adapters behind feature flag
Perf dashboards annotated and alert thresholds set
Compatibility shim created and EOL schedule communicated
